name: Barbell Bench Press
cues: Set the shoulder blades back and down against the bench.
Lower the bar to the mid-chest with elbows about 45 degrees from the torso.
Drive the feet into the floor and press the bar back over the shoulders.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Lifting the hips off the bench to move the load.

variations.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
variations.note: Greater range of motion and independent arm control.

variations.name: Push-Up
variations.note: Bodyweight regression that trains the same pressing pattern.

variations.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
variations.note: Narrower grip shifts emphasis to the triceps.

name: Pull-Up
cues: Start from a full hang with shoulders active, not slack.
Pull the elbows down and back to bring the chest toward the bar.
Control the descent all the way back to a straight-arm hang.
commonMistakes: Kipping or swinging to generate momentum.
Stopping short of full extension at the bottom.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.

variations.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
variations.note: A band offloads part of your bodyweight.

variations.name: Lat Pulldown
variations.note: Machine version with adjustable load.

variations.name: Weighted Pull-Up
variations.note: Add load via a belt once bodyweight reps are easy.

name: Barbell Back Squat
cues: Brace the core and keep the whole foot planted.
Break at the hips and knees together, sitting down between the legs.
Descend to at least parallel, then drive the floor away to stand.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward on the way up.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Rising onto the toes and shifting weight forward.

variations.name: Goblet Squat
variations.note: Front-loaded and easier to learn.

variations.name: Front Squat
variations.note: Bar on the front rack shifts load onto the quads.

variations.name: Box Squat
variations.note: A box sets a consistent depth target.

name: Conventional Deadlift
cues: Set the bar over mid-foot and take the slack out before pulling.
Keep a neutral spine and the lats tight to hold the bar close.
Push the floor away and finish by standing tall with locked hips.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back under load.
Letting the bar drift away from the shins.
Jerking the bar off the floor instead of building tension first.

variations.name: Trap-Bar Deadlift
variations.note: Neutral handles are friendlier to the lower back.

variations.name: Rack Pull
variations.note: Shortened range from pins for heavier loading.

variations.name: Deficit Deadlift
variations.note: Standing on a plate adds range of motion.

name: Standing Overhead Press
cues: Start with the bar on the front of the shoulders and elbows under the bar.
Brace the core and glutes to keep the torso from arching.
Press straight up and shrug the shoulders once the bar clears the head.
commonMistakes: Leaning back into a standing incline press.
Pressing the bar forward instead of overhead.
Failing to lock out fully at the top.

variations.name: Seated Dumbbell Press
variations.note: Seated and supported for more shoulder isolation.

variations.name: Push Press
variations.note: A leg drive lets you move heavier loads.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
cues: Hinge to roughly 45 degrees with a flat back.
Pull the bar to the lower ribs, leading with the elbows.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
commonMistakes: Standing up more upright as the set fatigues.
Yanking with the arms instead of the back.
Rounding the spine under the load.

variations.name: Chest-Supported Row
variations.note: A bench removes lower-back strain.

variations.name: Pendlay Row
variations.note: Each rep resets on the floor for strict power.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
cues: Keep the elbows pinned at the sides.
Curl through a full range and squeeze at the top.
Lower under control for two to three seconds.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to heave the weight up.
Letting the elbows drift forward.
Using only a partial range of motion.

variations.name: Hammer Curl
variations.note: Neutral grip adds forearm emphasis.

variations.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
variations.note: Reclined position increases the stretch.

name: Front Plank
cues: Stack the elbows under the shoulders.
Squeeze the glutes and brace as if bracing for a punch.
Keep a straight line from the ears to the heels.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
Piking the hips up into an easy position.
Holding the breath instead of breathing steadily.

variations.name: Knee Plank
variations.note: From the knees to reduce the load.

variations.name: Long-Lever Plank
variations.note: Elbows further forward greatly raises difficulty.

name: Standing Calf Raise
cues: Balls of the feet on the edge of a step.
Drop the heels for a full stretch, then rise onto the toes.
Pause briefly at the top of each rep.
commonMistakes: Bouncing through a shortened range.
Rushing reps without a peak contraction.
Bending the knees to cheat the movement.

variations.name: Seated Calf Raise
variations.note: Bent knee shifts work toward the soleus.

variations.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
variations.note: One leg doubles the relative load.

name: Romanian Deadlift
cues: Start standing tall with a soft bend in the knees.
Push the hips back and slide the bar down the thighs.
Feel the hamstring stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand.
commonMistakes: Turning it into a squat by bending the knees too much.
Rounding the back as the bar passes the knees.
Going lower than hamstring flexibility allows.

variations.name: Single-Leg RDL
variations.note: Adds a balance and stability challenge.

variations.name: Dumbbell RDL
variations.note: Dumbbells make the pattern easy to learn.

name: Zone 2 Run
cues: Hold an easy, conversational pace you could sustain for an hour.
Breathe rhythmically through the nose where possible.
Keep a relaxed, upright posture with a quick cadence.
commonMistakes: Drifting too fast so it becomes a moderate-hard effort.
Overstriding and landing heavily on the heels.
Skipping easy volume in favour of only hard sessions.

variations.name: Zone 2 Cycling
variations.note: Low-impact alternative on a bike.

variations.name: Brisk Incline Walk
variations.note: Lower-intensity entry point for beginners.

name: HIIT Intervals
cues: Warm up thoroughly before the first hard interval.
Push near-maximal effort for the work bout, then recover fully.
Keep work and rest periods consistent across the session.
commonMistakes: Starting too hard and fading across the set.
Cutting recovery short so power drops off.
Doing high-intensity work on consecutive days without recovery.

variations.name: Bike Sprint Intervals
variations.note: Low-impact, easy to control effort.

variations.name: 4x4 Intervals
variations.note: Four-minute efforts proven to raise VO2max.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
cues: Lie down with one hand on the chest and one on the belly.
Inhale slowly so the belly rises while the chest stays still.
Exhale longer than you inhale, fully emptying the lungs.
commonMistakes: Breathing high into the chest and shoulders.
Rushing the exhale.
Tensing the neck and jaw during the breath.

variations.name: Box Breathing
variations.note: Equal counts to inhale, hold, exhale, hold.

variations.name: Seated Diaphragmatic Breathing
variations.note: Practise the pattern upright once it is familiar.
